subject: LaunchPad private deployment: connectivity kickoff & staging plan
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Tanner <alex.tanner@launchpadlabs.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-20T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: LaunchPad private deployment: connectivity kickoff & staging plan

Alex — thanks again for choosing Redwood for your private deployment. This thread will be our primary connectivity and networking coordination channel while we scope staging and the on‑prem package for LaunchPad Labs. I’ve included Monica (CSM) and Karthik (network/infra) from our side so we can move quickly.

Quick overview / asks to unblock planning:
- Can you confirm the VPC CIDR(s) you want peered and the AWS account IDs?
- Are you planning to use a Transit Gateway or VPC peering for the production path?
- Do you expect to host the edge appliance on‑prem (we call it the edge appliance) or in a colocated environment? If on‑prem, please include the site public IP range and NAT/Egress constraints.
- Any corporate firewall/proxy rules we should expect (blocked ports, deep packet inspection)?
- Preferred week for staging cutover (we typically allow a 2‑week staging window followed by a 48h canary).

Attached: networking-preflight-template.xlsx (template for inventory), sample peering snippets we usually apply, and a short MQA (minimum QA) checklist. If you can populate the sheet and send back, Karthik and I will draft the peering runbook and firewall ACLs.

Proposed next steps:
1) Alex fills inventory + returns by EOD Tues (2026-11-24)
2) Karthik publishes peering/snippets and a proposed staging schedule by Thurs
3) We schedule a 60‑minute network review call the week of 11/30 to finalize the plan

Thanks — looking forward to getting LaunchPad onto a private instance.

—
Rachel Kim
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555‑0182

From: Alex Tanner <alex.tanner@launchpadlabs.com>

Cc: infra@launchpadlabs.com
Date: 2026-11-21T11:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: LaunchPad private deployment: connectivity kickoff & staging plan

Rachel / Monica — thanks, appreciate the clear checklist. Attached is our initial inventory (launchpad-network-inventory.csv) with the VPC and on‑prem details. Key items called out:
- Prod VPC CIDR: 10.40.0.0/16 (Account: 987654321098)
- Staging VPC CIDR: 10.41.0.0/16 (Account: 987654321098)
- We prefer Transit Gateway for production; peering ok for staging if the config is simpler.
- On‑prem site: Palo Alto WA‑SLC site, public egress IP block 35.201.12.0/24. Edge appliance will be hosted in our SLC colo (rack/space already reserved).
- Firewall: outbound to Redwood cluster needs TCP 443 and UDP 123 only; we do TLS inspection but will add exceptions for the appliance certificate chain.

We can target the week of 2026‑12‑07 for staging (two weeks is good). I’ve looped infra@launchpadlabs.com for any deep‑tech questions.

Short note: our procurement team will need a checklist of required certs (SOC2 attestation pointer) and the private endpoint IP range you anticipate, so we can reserve space on our end.

Cheers,
Alex Tanner
Director of Platform Engineering, LaunchPad Labs
alex.tanner@launchpadlabs.com

Attachments: launchpad-network-inventory.csv (CSV stub)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Tanner <alex.tanner@launchpadlabs.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-22T14:10:00-08:00
Subject: Re: LaunchPad private deployment: connectivity kickoff & staging plan

Thanks Alex — inventory looks clean. A few technical notes and actions from our infra team: 

1) Transit Gateway vs. VPC peering: we agree TGW for prod is the right call (scales with multi‑AZ and future multi‑account expansion). For staging we can use VPC peering to keep config simple.

2) Peering config snippets and iptables/NAT notes attached (redwood-peering-snippets.txt). Please reserve the following private endpoint ranges on your side: 172.31.200.0/24 (control plane), 172.31.201.0/24 (canary/staging private endpoints). These are internal only and not advertised to the internet.

3) Firewall rules: allow TCP 443 inbound from 35.201.12.0/24 to the appliance management port 8443; allow outbound TCP 443 to our cluster egress hosts (we will provide a short-lived list the week before cutover). Please also allow UDP 123 for NTP to our NTP pool. If your TLS inspection is altering certificates, please apply a pass‑through for the appliance certificate chain — we will provide the cert thumbprints.

4) NAT/eProxy: If your outbound egress is via a corporate proxy, we recommend configuring the appliance to use SNAT to the public egress IP (listed in your inventory) and whitelisting that IP on our side.

5) Staging plan: Proposed windows:
   - Provisioning & peering setup: 2026‑12‑07 to 2026‑12‑09
   - Dry run & smoke tests: 2026‑12‑10 to 2026‑12‑13
   - Canary production traffic ramp: 2026‑12‑14 to 2026‑12‑16

I created INFRA-7892 in our Jira and linked the runbook (see related links). If you can confirm the endpoint reservations and proxy behavior by 11/25 we can lock the provisioning window.

—
Karthik Iyer
Network Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com
